chunks: And from his words (peace be upon him): He said to al-Ash'ath ibn Qays while he was on the pulpit of Kufah delivering a sermon,
something of his speech was interrupted by al-Ash'ath, so he said: 'O Commander of the Faithful, this is against you, not for you.' So he (peace be upon him) lowered his gaze to him and then said:

key_terms.أَمِيرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful, a title primarily associated with Imam Ali (peace be upon him).
key_terms.الْأَشْعَثُ بْنُ قَيْسٍ: Al-Ash'ath ibn Qays, a prominent companion and later governor known for his eloquence and occasional opposition to Ali.
key_terms.خَفَضَ بَصَرَهُ: He lowered his gaze, indicating composure, humility, or a measured response.
key_terms.مَنْبَرِ الْكُوفَةِ: The pulpit of Kufah, the central platform for public sermons and announcements in the city of Kufah.

ai.seo_question: How did Imam Ali (peace be upon him) react when al-Ash'ath ibn Qays interrupted his sermon in Kufah?
ai.summary: This incident, recorded in Nahj al-Balagha, highlights Imam Ali’s (AS) psychological mastery and composure during his sermon in Kufah when challenged by the ambitious al-Ash'ath ibn Qays. The Imam’s response—lowering his gaze before speaking—demonstrates the Shia scholarly emphasis on *hilm* (forbearance) and dignified authority, showing that a leader’s reaction to interruption is a test of spiritual presence rather than mere rhetorical defense. This moment underscores the dynamic between the Caliphate’s public legitimacy and the internal political tensions with key Kufan commanders.
